newsitem.title: USA: Artichoke extract found to prevent some skin tumors.
newsitem.headline: Artichoke extract found to prevent some skin tumors.

text.p: An extract from artichokes rubbed on the skin of mice that were then exposed to ultraviolet rays sharply reduced the formation of skin tumors, researchers said Wednesday.

Only one-quarter of the mice treated with the compound silymarin developed tumors, compared to all the mice in a control group, said researchers at Case Western Reserve University and University Hospitals of Cleveland.
They published their study in this month's issue of the Journal of the National Cancer Institute.
Silymarin, which has not been studied on humans, is found in artichokes and other plants in the milk thistle family.

The compound only works when rubbed on the skin, not ingested, and represents one of several naturally occurring chemicals that have shown promise as cancer fighters, including green tea and vitamin E, the researchers said.
